subject: Privacy terms & audit access — final DPA execution and evidence packet
messages:
From: Jennie Torres <jennie.torres@medicorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medicorp.com>, Aaron Lim <aaron.lim@hoganlaw.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA questions and SOC 2 packet request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the baseline DPA. A few quick items from our legal and infosec teams:
- Can you confirm which subprocessors are currently in scope and whether Redwood has any planned changes in the next 6 months?
- MediCorp needs confirmation on audit rights: we require the ability to request evidence (SOC 2 report, pen test executive summary) and — in exceptional cases — rely on an independent auditor review. Is that permitted under Redwood's DPA?
- For data transfers from EU/UK patients, do you rely on SCCs, and can you provide the text reference in the DPA?

I've attached our vendor intake form — we also need the SOC 2 summary and the latest pen test summary. Procurement will need a signed DPA and DocuSign envelope for countersignature.

Best,
Jennie
Head of Vendor Risk
MediCorp Health

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jennie Torres <jennie.torres@medicorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions and SOC 2 packet request

Jennie — thanks, got it. Attaching our redlines to the DPA and the compliance packet (SOC 2 summary + pen test executive summary). See attachments.

Quick answers:
- Subprocessors: current list included in section 6 of the DPA; no planned changes currently, but we’ll notify with 30 days prior notice and an objection window.
- Audit rights: Redwood provides SOC 2 reports and pen test summaries on request. For on-site or independent auditor reviews, we permit them under narrow conditions — needs prior notice, agreed scope, and reasonable redaction to protect other customers and our infrastructure details. I’ve flagged Laura to add formal language.
- Transfers: we rely on EU SCCs and, where customers require, we can add a data transfer appendix referencing the current SCCs.

Attachments: MediCorp_DPA_redlines_20260312.docx; SOC2-summary-2025.pdf; pen-test-summary-2025.pdf

Next steps: Laura will propose final DPA language on the audit and subprocessor clauses. If Procurement signs off on the redlines, we’ll prepare a DocuSign envelope and route to your procurement team.

Thanks — talk soon,
Karthik
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jennie Torres <jennie.torres@medicorp.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial DPA questions and SOC 2 packet request

Jennie — hi, Laura from Redwood legal. I reviewed your ask and Karthik’s redlines and propose the following compromise language for audit rights to include in the DPA: 

"Customer may request access to Redwood's SOC 2 report and summary pen test reports. For audit activities beyond review of provided artifacts (e.g., independent on-site audits), Customer must provide 45 days' notice, define the scope in writing and execute a mutually agreeable NDA and MSA addendum limiting access to Redwood's proprietary material and other customers' data. Such audits may be subject to reasonable fees to cover third-party logistics and security oversight."

On subprocessors, we will: provide the current list in an appendix, notify customers 30 days in advance of material changes, and allow customers to object if a subprocessor cannot meet their lawful requirements. If objection cannot be resolved, Customer may terminate affected Services on a pro rata basis.

Mina — please confirm that the evidence packet we provided covers the infosec questions.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

---

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jennie Torres <jennie.torres@medicorp.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial DPA questions and SOC 2 packet request

Jennie — thanks for the request. The attached SOC 2 summary and pen test executive summary provide the high-level evidence Procurement usually needs; they do not include detailed vulnerability lists. For customers requiring deeper evidence, we offer an NDA-based sharing process for a limited set of artifacts.

Regarding subprocessors: current critical subprocessors are listed in the appendix (cloud infra provider, observability provider, embedding store). None handle unredacted customer content besides the infra provider. We follow key management options (bring-your-own-key available for Dedicated/Private customers).

If MediCorp needs KMS integration or a private deployment for additional isolation, we can outline options and an estimated timeline.

- Mina
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pen-test-summary-2025.pdf
